text: This man just stepped into quicksand, and it's pulling him down.
He panics and kicks, but moving makes the sand go runny, so he sinks deeper.
When he stops, the sand settles and packs tight around his legs.
Here's the good news: he can't sink all the way under.
Quicksand is about twice as heavy as his body, so he floats near his waist.
The bad news? Pulling one foot out slowly takes about the force of lifting a car.
And on a beach, the real danger is the tide coming in while he's stuck.
So he wiggles his legs slowly, so water seeps back in and loosens the sand.
Then he leans back, floats flat, and inches his way to solid ground.
And that's what really happens when you step in quicksand.
